# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 17 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Son of David — The Messianic King

---

**17:1** O LORD, you are our king forever and ever;
in you, O God, our soul takes its glory.

**17:2** How brief is the span of a man's life on earth;
as long as his days, so great is his hope.

**17:3** But we hope in God our savior;
for the strength of our God endures forever in mercy,
and the kingdom of our God rules over the nations forever in judgment.

**17:4** You, O LORD, chose David as king over Israel
and swore to him concerning his seed forever,
that his kingdom would never fail before you.

**17:5** But because of our sins, sinners rose up against us,
they attacked and expelled us —
those to whom you had made no promise;
they plundered with force and did not give glory to your holy name.

**17:6** In arrogance they established a kingdom
and laid waste the throne of David with riotous pride.

**17:7** But you, O God, cast them down and took away their seed from the earth,
for against them rose a man who was alien to our race.

**17:8** You repaid them, O God, according to their sins;
it came upon them according to their deeds.

**17:9** God showed them no mercy;
he tracked down their seed and did not let a single one go free.

**17:10** Faithful is the LORD in all his judgments
that he executes on the earth.

**17:11** The lawless one laid waste our land,
so that there was none who practiced mercy and truth.

**17:12** They withdrew to a place of desolation;
they came nowhere near our territory.

**17:13** The enemy acted with arrogance,
and his heart was alienated from our God.

**17:14** And everything he was doing in Jerusalem
was what the nations were doing in their own fortified cities.

**17:15** And the children of the covenant, dwelling in the midst of the mixed peoples,
none of them in Jerusalem practiced mercy or truth.

**17:16** Those who had loved the assemblies of the devout fled from them;
like sparrows they flew away from their nest.

**17:17** They wandered in deserts to save their souls from evil;
and the soul that was saved was precious in the eyes of any exile among them.

**17:18** They were scattered throughout every land by the lawless one;
for the sky withheld its dew and rain from falling on the earth.

**17:19** Perennial springs were dried up,
which spring from the depths to the high mountains;
for no one among them did righteousness and justice.

**17:20** Their leaders were killed by the sword;
no one mourned for them,
for they were strangers.

**17:21** Behold, O LORD, and raise up for them their king,
the son of David, at the time you know, O God,
to reign over Israel your servant.

**17:22** Gird him with strength to shatter unrighteous rulers,
to purge Jerusalem from the nations that trample her down to ruin.

**17:23** In wisdom, in righteousness, let him drive sinners out from the inheritance;
let him smash the arrogance of the sinner like a potter's vessel.

**17:24** With a rod of iron let him break all their substance to pieces;
with the word of his mouth let him destroy the lawless nations.

**17:25** At his rebuke let the nations flee before him;
let him convict sinners by the thoughts of their own hearts.

**17:26** Let him gather a holy people
whom he shall lead in righteousness,
and let him judge the tribes of the people sanctified by the LORD his God.

**17:27** He shall not permit unrighteousness to lodge among them;
nor shall any man who knows wickedness dwell in their midst.

**17:28** For he shall know them — that they are all children of their God —
and he shall apportion them over the land according to their tribes.

**17:29** Neither sojourner nor alien shall dwell among them any longer.
He shall judge peoples and nations in the wisdom of his righteousness. Selah.

**17:30** He shall have the Gentile nations serve him under his yoke;
and he shall glorify the LORD in a place visible to all the earth;

**17:31** and he shall purify Jerusalem, making it holy as it was in the days of old,

**17:32** so that nations may come from the ends of the earth to behold his glory,
bringing as gifts her sons who had been cast out,

**17:33** and to see the glory of the LORD, with which God has glorified her.
And he shall be a righteous king over them, taught by God.

**17:34** There will be no unrighteousness in his days in their midst,
for all shall be holy and their king is the LORD Messiah.

**17:35** For he will not place his confidence in horse and rider and bow;
he will not amass gold and silver for war,

**17:36** nor will he gather hope from a multitude for the day of battle.
The LORD himself is his king, the hope of the one mighty through hope in God.

**17:37** He will be merciful to all the nations who stand before him in fear.

**17:38** For he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth forever;
he will bless the people of the LORD with wisdom and gladness.

**17:39** He will himself be pure from sin, to rule over a great people,
rebuking rulers and purging sinners by the power of his word.

**17:40** He will not grow faint in his days, relying upon his God;
for God has made him strong in the Holy Spirit
and wise in the counsel of understanding,
with strength and righteousness.

**17:41** The blessing of the LORD is with him in power;
and his hope in the LORD will not waver.

**17:42** Who will prevail against him?
He is mighty in his works and strong in the fear of God;

**17:43** he tends the flock of the LORD in faithfulness and righteousness;
he lets none of them stumble in their pasture.

**17:44** He leads them all in equity;
there is no arrogance among them to oppress any.

**17:45** This is the majesty of the king of Israel,
whom God knows and raises up over the house of Israel to instruct it.

**17:46** His words are as the words of the holy ones, in the midst of holy peoples.
Blessed are those who shall be born in those days,
to see the good things of Israel which God shall accomplish
in the gathering together of the tribes.
May God hasten his mercy upon Israel!
May he deliver us from the pollution of those who are profane enemies!
The LORD himself is our king forever and ever.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal rendering of Ps 17. This psalm shaped the entire messianic expectation of Second Temple Judaism and early Christianity. 'The LORD Messiah' (v.34) rendered as 'LORD Messiah' following Greek Christos Kyrios.*
